sentence: This project tests whether ants that form huge supercolonies in invasive ranges show genomic degradation compared with ants from their native range.
This project studies how cells find and remove faulty ribosomes and how zebrafish cartilage develops when this process fails.
This project tries to overcome photobleaching and limited readout in qubits made from fluorescent proteins, so they can work at the single-molecule level.
This project builds AI systems that copy the large 3D world from real videos and simulate what would happen under different decisions.
This project studies how proteins that decorate microtubules control which kinesin motors can move along them inside cells.
This project tests whether cold exposure early in life changes how wild birds cope with changing temperatures later, in individuals and in populations.
This project builds a tiny AI chip that reads vibration and sound signals to spot when motors in drones and robots may fail.
This project builds a sensitive tool that uses lasers to measure how fast cells crawl through living tissues and which drugs stop cancer cells from spreading.
This project studies how flexible floating structures respond to ordinary and breaking waves, using large-scale experiments and computational simulations.
This project builds a system that profiles open-source multi-modal large language models, recommends ones that fit a science task, and adds safeguards for food science.
This project studies a portable sensor that detects chemical markers of colorectal cancer in breath or urine as a low-cost screening test.
This project brings together researchers from two polymer science programs to design and make synthetic materials inspired by nature.
This project develops mathematical methods for simulating how fluids and structures influence each other, aiming to preserve volume and give accurate local forces.
This project studies why stalks of cereal crops break before harvest and builds tools to help breeders develop sturdier varieties.
This project studies when efficient algorithms cannot reach information-theoretic limits for statistical tasks and builds mathematical tools to show it.
This project uses computer simulations and telescopes to study stars that combine a cold red supergiant outside with a neutron core inside.
This project studies carbon-based materials with interesting electrical properties and builds nanomaterials that work as sensors for metals and organic pollutants.
